Rh-Catalyzed cyclization of 2,3-allenoic acids
in the presence of 2,3-allenols †‡
Junjie Fan,
 a Chunling Fu, a Xiaoyan Wu
 *ab and Shengming Ma
 *ab
Herein we report a [Cp*RhCl 2]2-catalyzed coupling cyclization of
two diﬀerent classes of allenes with 2,3-allenoic acids aﬀording
2(5H)-furanone skeletons of products and 2,3-allenols forming a
conjugated (E)-enal or enone functionality to the b-position of the
2(5H)-furanones. These products are important building blocks for
the syntheses of potentially bioactive compounds. The reaction
proceeded via the nucleometalation, insertion, and stereodefined
1,4-H delivery carried by rhodium.
Over the past few decades, the chemistry of allenes has been
receiving more and more attention. 1 Now it has become a
common approach to construct diﬀerent types of cyclic struc-
tures with synthetic or bio-potentials via the cyclizations of
allenes with a nucleophilic functionality.
2–4 Recently, Rh-
catalyzed cyclization of two molecules of the same 2,3-allenols
was reported to afford (2,5-dihydrofuran-3-yl)but-2-( E)-en-1-one
derivatives A (Scheme 1a).
5 Here we envisioned such a bimole-
cular allene cyclization reaction of two different types of
allenes. In the first place, we wished to attempt the cyclization
of 2,3-allenoic acids in the presence of 2,3-allenols. There are
intricate challenges: (1) as expected, both homo-coupling cycli-
zation 2,5-dihydrofuran products A and E or the cyclizative
cross-coupling furanone products B
4a and D may be formed
(Scheme 1b); (2) in addition, the cycloisomerization products
C4b and F4c may also be formed. We wish to report here a highly
selective protocol of the cyclizative cross-coupling of allenoic
acids in the presence of 2,3-allenols to construct a new type of
furanone derivatives, which are common units existing in many
bioactive compounds and natural products, for instance, ascor-
bic acid (vitamin C),
6 the selective COX-2 inhibitor: Rofecoxib, 7
digitalis extracts: digitoxigenin 8 etc. (Scheme 1c).
We began our studies on the reaction of 2,3-allenoic acid 1a
and 2,3-allenol 2a under the conditions for the homo-cyclizative
coupling products of allenols (Scheme 2). 5 The reaction did
aﬀord the homo-coupling product ( E)-3a in 9% NMR yield
derived from two molecules of 2,3-allenol 2a. In addition, the
desired cross-over cyclizative coupling product ( E)-4aa was
formed in 29% NMR yield. The B-type diene product 5aa and
cycloisomerization product 6a and 7a were not detected.
In order to optimize the selectivity for the formation of a cross-
coupling product (E)-4aa,C u C l2/C12H2O, Cu(NO3)2 and CuO were
applied as the oxidants to replace Cu(OAc)2/C1H2O under a nitrogen

Thus, we defined the conditions of entry 7 for highly selective
formation of (E)-4.
The reaction scope under optimal conditions was then
investigated. Furanone derivatives containing the synthetically
versatile a,b-enals and enones ( E)-4 were synthesized highly
E-selectively (Table 2). R
1 groups of 2,3-allenoic acids may be
n-octyl, 3-chloropropyl, phenethyl, and benzyl, reacting with
allenol 2a to aﬀord ( E)-4ba,( E)-4ca,( E)-4da, and ( E)-4ea in
48–61% yields. When R2 are 1 1-alkyl or 2 1-alkyl groups, the
reaction with 2,3-allenoic acid 1a gave moderate yields of
(E)-4aa,( E)-4ab,( E)-4ad, and ( E)-4ae. Functionalized allenols
with R2 being 5-chloropentyl, terminal C QC bond, and benzyl
protected hydroxyl showed decent reactivity to afford ( E)-4ac,
(E)-4af, and (E)-4ag in 49–56% yields. Phenyl and halogen atom-
substituted (F, Cl, Br) on the para-, ortho-o rmeta -position of
the benzene ring could all be tolerated to afford ( E)-4ah–(E)-
4am in 43–66% yields. We confirmed the structure of the
products by single crystal of 4ai. 2-Furyl-substituted allenol
2n also could react with allenoic acid 1a to produce ( E)-4an in
47% yield. In addition, a,b-unsaturated enal ( E)-4ao may be
prepared from buta-2,3-dien-1-ol 2o and 1a in 33% yield.

To further explore the synthetic utility of this methodology,
the reactions were conducted on 5 mmol scale under standard
conditions to aﬀord ( E)-4ai in 52% yield. ( E)-4ai could be
reduced to an E-selective allyl alcohol ( E)-9 by treatment with
sodium borohydride (Scheme 3, eqn (1)). When the oxygen
atmosphere was replaced with an air atmosphere, the reaction
worked similarly, aﬀording ( E)-4ai in 54% yield (Scheme 3,
eqn (2)).
To clarify the mechanism, an isotopic labelling experiment
was conducted (Scheme 3, eqn (3)): the reaction of allenoic acid
1a and deuterated allenol [D]-2a (499% D) under standard
conditions aﬀorded [D]-( E)-4aa with the methyl connected to
the sp
2 carbon atom being mono-deuterated, indicating the
possibility of a 1,4-H delivery pathway. 10
Based on the experimental results and our previous studies,
a mechanism was proposed as shown in Scheme 4. At first, the
allenoic acid 1 went through a nucleophilic cyclic oxyrhodation
to aﬀord 2-oxo-2,5-dihydrofuran-4-yl rhodium intermediate
IN-1. Subsequently the allene unit in deuterated allenol [D]- 2
underwent syn-insertion into the carbon–rhodium bond and
the OH group coordinated with Rh to generate the stereo-
defined allylic rhodium intermediate IN-2. The deuterated
allylic rhodium hydride IN-3 was formed by deprotonation of
the hydroxyl group mediated by an allenoate anion 10 and b-D
elimination. IN-3 would yield [D]-( E)-4 and Rh( I) species via
reductive elimination. The Rh( I) species would be oxidized to
Rh(III)b yO 2 to finish the catalytic cycle. 11
In conclusion, the Rh(III)-catalyzed highly chemoselective cycli-
zative cross-coupling of 2,3-allenoic acids with 2,3-allenols aﬀord-
ing 4-(4
0-oxo-20-en-20-yl)-2(5H)-furanone derivatives was established.
The reaction proceededvia cyclic nucleometalation, insertion, and
stereodefined 1,4-H delivery as unveiled by mechanistic studies.
Further studies in this area are currently ongoing in this laboratory.
